scene.title: Kerala Backwater Kitchen Courtyard
scene.blurb: A lively semi-open kitchen courtyard typical of Kerala's backwater homes, featuring brass vessels, spice trays, coconut husking tools, and smoke-darkened rafters. This scene strongly conveys the sensory environment of a
scene.summary: This diorama captures the everyday semi-open kitchen courtyard in a traditional Kerala backwater home. It combines locally sourced materials like timber and terracotta with culturally specific artifacts such as the brass uruli pots, spice trays arranged in a tiled nook, and implements used for coconut processing, anchored spatially by the smoke-dark rafters above. Functional surfaces are layered with tools, vessels, and textiles showing daily food-prep rituals.

details.title: Brass Uruli Vessels
details.body: Traditional shallow, wide brass vessels known locally as uruli, prominently used for cooking, heating, and serving in Kerala. Their warm golden patina and evidence of use reflect the historic local metalcraft and copper alloy economy. They sit on wooden shelves and the terracotta floor, creating a strong textural contrast.

details.title: Spice Tray Niche
details.body: A built-in niche tiled with warm terracotta in the plaster wall holds banana leaf-lined trays filled with turmeric powder, red chili powder, mustard seeds, and dried curry leaves. This practical design keeps essential spices within reach, dryer and away from pests, reflecting Kerala's culinary emphasis on layered spice blends.

details.title: Coconut Husking and Grating Tools
details.body: Wooden tools designed specifically for detaching the coconut husk and grating the fresh kernel are arranged on a low bench next to a clay grinding stone with a brass pestle. This workspace is dedicated to coconut processing, a staple ingredient in Kerala cuisine and daily life.

details.title: Smoke-Darkened Roof Rafters
details.body: Exposed timber rafters overhead are deeply darkened by centuries of smoke from open woodfires used for cooking. This feature reflects the semi-open nature of traditional Kerala kitchen courtyards, with natural ventilation and historical fuel use.

details.title: Terracotta Paved Floor and Plastered Walls
details.body: The floor is paved with warm terracotta tiles with wear visible in high traffic zones. Walls are smoothly plastered with a lime-based earthy pigment. This natural palette grounds the space in Kerala’s vernacular architectural traditions and climate adaptations.
